summary: Remote-controlled PTY shell and filesystem access driven by a configurable WebSocket server
details: The package's agent binary (yeaft-agent) opens a persistent WebSocket connection to a configured server and dispatches incoming messages to handlers that give the remote peer full control over the host. The `terminal_create` handler spawns a PTY shell (`pty.spawn(process.env.SHELL || 'bash',...)` on Linux/macOS, PowerShell/cmd on Windows) and `terminal_input` writes bytes received from the server directly into that PTY (`term.pty.write(msg.data)`), with the shell's stdout streamed back over the WebSocket. Additional message handlers perform arbitrary file read/write, git operations, Claude CLI invocations, and an `upgrade_agent` action that runs `npm view @yeaft/webchat-agent@latest version` and then executes a script performing `npm install @yeaft/webchat-agent@latest` followed by a systemd/launchd/PM2 service restart. Although the default `SERVER_URL` is `ws://localhost:3456`, it is overridable via environment variable and stored configuration, so the agent can be pointed at any remote WebSocket endpoint, at which point the operator of that endpoint has interactive shell, arbitrary filesystem access, and unpinned self-update control over every host running the agent. `service/linux.js` also configures a service PATH including `~/.local/bin`, `~/.npm-global/bin`, and system directories, so the shell executes with the installing user's full toolchain in scope.
